architecture.mechanism: Real-time dynamic bus holding times at stops, computed by optimization, to counteract headway instability and prevent buses of the same line from cruising head-to-tail or arriving simultaneously.
architecture.intervention: Add a real-time headway-control layer to the existing route control system that tracks each bus's position/headway and computes optimal holding times at stops (linear objective minimizing bunching penalties under quadratic constraints, solved with a beam-search heuristic for sub-3-second decisions on 60-bus instances), holding early/fast buses at control stops until the target headway is restored — no additional vehicles required.
architecture.expected_effect: Significantly reduced bus bunching and more evenly spaced arrivals, with shorter average passenger waiting times, all at constant fleet size.
architecture.falsification_test: On one route, run the holding-time controller in an A/B trial (controller active vs. inactive) across matched service periods and measure the coefficient of variation of headways at high-demand stops plus bunching events per day; the mechanism is falsified if active control does not significantly reduce headway variance and bunching frequency versus baseline.
